description: We are Azurix, a team of young innovators passionate about technology, space exploration, and problem-solving. Led by Ali Ahmed, we aim to turn creative ideas into impactful solutions using NASA's open data and resources. We're looking for web developers, AI enthusiasts, video editors, graphic designers, and researchers. We value creativity, teamwork, curiosity, and commitment. Join Azurix and let's explore beyond the ordinary!
summary:
Reliquenix is an interactive web platform designed to preserve and explore humanity’s space heritage by documenting abandoned spacecraft, equipment, and vehicles left behind on the Moon and Mars. Inspired by NASA’s “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, the platform brings scattered information about these objects together in one accessible experience.

Through an interactive map, users can explore the locations of abandoned space objects and discover their names, purposes, associated missions, and historical significance. By combining exploration with educational storytelling, Reliquenix transforms forgotten mission hardware into meaningful stories about humanity’s journey into space.

Our project aims to raise awareness of the scientific and historical value of these objects, make space exploration more accessible and engaging, and preserve the legacy of past missions for future generations. We believe that space exploration is not only about reaching new destinations but also about remembering what we leave behind.
details:
Project Details – Reliquenix

Reliquenix is an interactive web platform developed to document, explore, and preserve humanity's space heritage, focusing on abandoned spacecraft, landers, rovers, and other human-made objects left on celestial bodies.

The platform aims to make information about these objects easier to discover and understand. Users can explore documented locations, learn about the missions associated with them, and discover the historical and scientific significance of each object through an accessible and engaging interface. By organizing information into a centralized experience, Reliquenix helps users understand what remains on the Moon and Mars and why these objects should not be forgotten.

The project's main benefit is combining space exploration, education, and historical preservation. It encourages curiosity about past space missions, raises awareness of humanity's physical footprint beyond Earth, and highlights the importance of preserving space heritage for future generations.

We developed Reliquenix as a web-based project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML structures the platform, CSS creates its visual identity and responsive interface, and JavaScript adds interactive functionality. We also used online research and available space exploration information to shape the project's content and concept.

What makes Reliquenix creative is its approach to abandoned space objects: instead of treating them simply as forgotten equipment, it presents them as historical evidence of human exploration. We wanted to turn scattered information into an engaging journey through space history.

During development, our team considered information accessibility, historical accuracy, ease of navigation, visual clarity, educational value, and the importance of communicating the significance of these objects to different audiences, including people with little prior knowledge of space exploration.
